title: Sales enablement: Enterprise prospect playbook — positioning, pricing, case studies, security FAQ
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview:

This enterprise prospect playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's positioning and messaging, competitive talking points, pitch deck outline, pricing guidance, exemplar case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospects evaluating inference platforms. Use this doc as the canonical single-page reference for AEs, SEs, and solutions architects running enterprise conversations and demos.

One-liner:
- Redwood Inference: a developer-first, production-grade inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable, cost-effective, and deployable across hosted, dedicated, and private environments.

Target audience and buyer personas:
- Engineering Lead / ML Infra Manager — cares about latency, reliability, and integration effort.
- Product Lead / Head of AI — cares about product velocity, model quality, and feature ROI.
- Platform / Security / Compliance — cares about data residency, auditability, and isolation.
- Procurement / Finance — cares about unit economics, predictable spend, and contract terms.

Top-level positioning pillars (elevator pitches):
1) Production-first economics: predictable per-token cost through batching, caching, and model routing so teams can scale features without surprise bills.
2) Unified runtime across environments: same API, tooling, and rollout controls for Hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
3) Reliability and graceful degradation: automated fallbacks (model variants, regions, tiers) and SLOs that keep customer experiences online during capacity or model regressions.

Key value propositions by persona (talking points):
- Engineering Lead: "Ship faster with a proven runtime — reduced latency and simple SDKs. We handle kernel selection, batching, and KV caching."
- Product Lead: "Deliver consistent UX across regions and scale: stable response quality, streaming, and function/tool calling."
- Platform/Security: "Bring your own VPC, integrate with KMS/HSM, and retain audit logs — Redwood Private supports compliance controls and on-prem packaging."
- Finance: "Lower TCO via intelligent batching and optimized kernels; dedicated capacity offers predictable commits with discounts."

Objection handling (short):
- "We can self-host cheaper": Explain hidden operational costs (benchmark, staffing, retries, SRE); highlight Redwood Optimize recommendations that typically reduce per-token cost 20–40% vs naive self-hosting.
- "Vendor lock-in concerns": Emphasize unified API + model abstraction, exportable configs, and private deployment options.
- "Security/compliance": Point to Redwood Private, audit logs, KMS, SOC/ISO compliance evidence (see security folder).

Competitive brief (summary of common competitors and callouts):
- Major cloud AI platforms (Cloud A, Cloud B):
  - Strengths: deep cloud integration, managed infra.
  - Redwood differentiators: finer-grained inference economics, open-model catalog, stronger developer tooling for model rollouts and per-route observability.
- LLM API providers (Provider X, Provider Y):
  - Strengths: simple API, turnkey models.
  - Redwood differentiators: deployment flexibility (dedicated/private), cost controls, and production-grade SLOs suitable for high-scale product features.
- Inference vendors / on-prem runtimes (Vendor Z):
  - Strengths: control and cost at scale for specialized teams.
  - Redwood differentiators: unified control plane, plug-and-play autoscaling policies, and built-in regressions/evals to protect quality during model updates.

Competitive talking points for SEs:
- If prospect values lowest-latency single-region inference: focus on Dedicated + node sizing and latency SLOs. Provide latency benchmarks for comparable models and sequence lengths.
- If prospect prioritizes compliance: lead with Redwood Private, KMS/HSM integration, audit logging, and evidence collection process.
- If prospect is cost-sensitive at scale: quantify savings from batching/caching/quantization; run a 1-week proof-of-concept with telemetry to produce a cost forecast.

Pitch deck: recommended 12-slide flow and speaker notes
1) Title + hook (1 slide) — 1-line problem statement + customer logo montage.
2) Problem (1 slide) — cost/latency/complexity of self-managed inference.
3) Why now (1 slide) — model improvements, open model ecosystem, and demands for production control.
4) Redwood overview (1 slide) — Hosted, Dedicated, Private + Console, Optimize.
5) Architecture (1 slide) — runtime, smart routing, caching, deployment abstraction (diagram).
6) Performance & economics (1 slide) — sample latency & cost curves for common model classes.
7) Security & compliance (1 slide) — KMS, audit logging, VPC, on-prem package.
8) Customer proofs (2 slides) — condensed case studies with metrics (latency improvement, cost reduction, time-to-production).
9) Pricing & commercial offers (1 slide) — starter pricing, enterprise commit options, add-ons.
10) Deployment & onboarding (1 slide) — implementation phases and timelines.
11) Customers & partners (1 slide) — logos and partner integrations.
12) Next steps & ask (1 slide) — trial, POC scope, decision timeline.

Speaker notes: keep technical audiences in slide 5–7 territory; finance/procurement focus on slide 6 and 9. For security audiences, expand slide 7 with architecture diagrams and compliance artifacts.

Pricing guidance (rules of thumb + example templates):
- Pricing components:
  - Hosted API: per-token generation + per-embedding unit; tiered volume discounts.
  - Dedicated: committed monthly/annual GPU pool with a baseline throughput SLA; overage pricing per request or token.
  - Private: enterprise licensing + support + optional installation fee.
  - Add-ons: observability retention, premium SLA, compliance packages (SOC/ISO evidence), extended support.

Example pricing templates (illustrative; customize per prospect):
- Starter (Hosted, SMB) — Pay-as-you-go:
  - Generation: $0.01 / 1K tokens
  - Embeddings: $0.02 / 1K units
  - No monthly commitment, 30-day support, self-serve onboarding

- Growth (Hosted with committed usage) — 12-month commit:
  - Base discount: 20% off list per-token rates for commits > $50k/month
  - Optional Premium Support: $5k/mo for 24/7 coverage

- Enterprise Dedicated — example (annual contract):
  - Reserved GPU pool for predicted peak throughput (billing monthly): $40k - $200k / month depending on fleet size and model mix
  - SLA: 99.9% uptime, latency targets defined per-route
  - Onboarding & integration fee: one-time $25k–$75k (scope dependent)

- Private deployment:
  - Platform license: annual fee (example $250k+) + professional services and support tiering.

Commercial play tips for AEs:
1) For technical POCs, propose a 4-week trial with scripted workload, telemetry integration, and a cost/latency report at the end.
2) Lock in model & route definitions for cost forecasts; call out variance when customers add longer sequences or multimodal usage.
3) Bundle observability + premium SLA for enterprise pilots to reduce friction.

Case studies (two concise examples):
1) NovaCRM (B2B SaaS) — objective: add AI-powered summarization to CRM threads
  - Deployment: Hosted -> Dedicated after 3 months
  - Results: 60% reduction in per-request latency (median 180ms -> 72ms), 35% unit-cost reduction after Redwood Optimize batching and quantization recommendations, production rollout in 8 weeks.
  - Key wins: preserved conversational quality via A/B evals, canary rollouts for model updates, saved $120k in ops vs in-house effort.

2) MediHealth (regulated healthcare workflow) — objective: clinical note extraction with PHI controls
  - Deployment: Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem inference nodes) with KMS integration
  - Results: met customer SOC/ISO evidence requirements, audit logs integrated with SIEM, achieved SLA-backed latency targets for critical routes, time-to-production 12 weeks including compliance validation.
  - Key wins: enabled data residency, explicit role-based access controls, and reduced audit scope for the customer by consolidating logging.

Security FAQ for prospects (short answers for common prospect concerns):
Q: Can we run Redwood in our VPC / on-prem?
A: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and a packaged on-prem deployment. We provide a customer-managed control plane option and professional services to validate networking and installation.

Q: How do you handle encryption and keys?
A: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM solutions (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, and on-prem HSMs). Keys for private deployments remain customer-managed; hosted customers can use Redwood-managed or customer-provided KMS.

Q: Is audit logging available?
A: Yes. We provide structured audit logs for request metadata, model version, route, and user identity. Logs can be forwarded to customer SIEMs or retained in Redwood Console per configured retention policies.

Q: How do you protect model/data lineage and PII?
A: We support data classification pipelines, prefix/KV caching controls, and optional masking at ingestion. For high-sensitivity workloads, we recommend Private deployments + service-level data handling agreements.

Q: What compliance evidence is available?
A: We maintain SOC/ISO evidence packages and a documented evidence collection process. For enterprise deals we run a tailored compliance onboarding checklist and provide artifacts for audits.

Q: How is tenant isolation implemented?
A: Tenant isolation is enforced at multiple layers: network (VPC, security groups), compute (dedicated GPU pools for Dedicated/Private), and logical controls (RBAC, per-tenant configs).

Onboarding checklist (recommended 8–12 week enterprise pilot):
1) Kickoff & scoping (week 1): agree on model variants, routes, data residency, and success metrics.
2) Environment setup (weeks 1–2): networking, KMS, and credentials.
3) Integration & telemetry (weeks 2–4): SDK integration, tracing, and metrics export.
4) Performance tuning (weeks 3–5): batch sizing, cache policies, and quantization recommendations.
5) Security/compliance validation (weeks 4–7): evidence collection and penetration testing if requested.
6) Pilot run & analysis (weeks 6–8): telemetry review, cost forecast, and quality evals.
7) Contract & rollout planning (weeks 9–12): finalize committed terms and dedicated/private provisioning.

- For enterprise conversations, loop in Security and Solutions Engineering by the first meeting.
- Save POC telemetry into the shared folder: /confluence/sales-enablement/poctrials (create a summary report and link to customer case file).

Appendix: example 4-week POC success metrics (KPIs to measure)
- Latency: median & 95th percentile per route.
- Cost: per-1000-token cost pre/post Redwood Optimize.
- Quality: A/B evaluation pass rate and model drift indicators.
- Reliability: error rate and successful failovers during simulated capacity events.
